blocks.text: “The naked male body circulates under two regimes: one that consumes it, one that sells it. Between them lies a space almost no one occupies. That is where I work — to look without possessing.” Topographie du désir reads the male body as a territory of light and relief, in six acts named after land-surveying terms. The men I photograph are not professional models; their ages and bodies differ deliberately, and none of them is identified. The series was published as a book in Montréal in August 2026; it is held in seven institutional collections, among them the Bishopsgate Institute in London, the Schwules Museum in Berlin and IHLIA LGBTI Heritage in Amsterdam. Patrick Bélanger is a photographer recently settled in Montréal. He has worked on the male nude since 2015.
